artists.biography: Knifeworld is the new band from Kavus Torabi (Cardiacs, The Monsoon Bassoon, Guapo). The forthcoming album also features a handful of special guests, including Ben Jacobs (Max Tundra) on trumpet, Melanie Woods (Sidi Bou Said, Cardiacs) on vocals, Katharine Blake (Miranda Sex Garden, Mediæval Bæbes) on recorders, Sarah Measures (The Monsoon Bassoon, Mothlite) on horns and flute, and Khyam Allami on drums. Pissed Up On Brake Fluid, the first Knifeworld single, will be released by Believers Roast on July 13th 2009. It is probably the closest thing to a 'straightforward rock song' Torabi has ever written. The B-side, Happy Half-life, Dear Friend is not. It's barely even rock. It is, however, extremely psychedelic. Forthcoming debut album, Buried Alone: Tales Of Crushing Defeat, is a sprawling psychedelic meisterwork, taking in elements of pop, heavy rock, hardcore, avant-progressive and folk, and is due out on August 10th 2009. Read more on Last.fm. User-contributed text is available under the Creative Commons By-SA License; additional terms may apply.

perplexity.description:
Knifeworld’s Bottled Out of Eden, released in 2016 on InsideOut Music, is a vibrant and ambitious studio album that blends progressive rock, psychedelic pop, and experimental rock into a distinctive sonic tapestry. Led by Kavus Torabi, Knifeworld crafts an eleven-track song cycle marked by intricate arrangements, lush harmonies, and a kaleidoscopic use of instrumentation, including flutes, horns, and layered guitars. The album’s sound is both melodic and adventurous, balancing accessible pop sensibilities with the complexity and unpredictability characteristic of progressive rock.

Within Knifeworld’s discography, Bottled Out of Eden stands as a mature and cohesive statement, showcasing the band’s evolution from their earlier, more fragmented works into a unified collective voice. The album explores themes of loss and hope, with each track contributing to an overarching narrative arc. Critics praised its creativity and emotional depth, noting its successful fusion of psychedelic textures and progressive structures. While not a mainstream commercial breakthrough, the album received strong acclaim in progressive and alternative music circles, solidifying Knifeworld’s reputation as innovators within the genre.
